title: Conditional unmasking for tenant-scoped traces with tiered retention and audit trail
creator: Aisha Kaur
description:
Scope: Implement an ingestion-time and query-time policy layer that performs conditional data unmasking for tenant-scoped traces and logs. The feature must: (1) apply deterministic redaction rules at ingest for sensitive fields, (2) retain multiple retention tiers (hot: 30d full-sampled sanitized events, cold: 365d aggregated/metrics-only), (3) allow on-demand, auditable unmasking of specific trace segments for authorized principals under RBAC and a short-lived reveal token, and (4) annotate latency/error dashboards so engineers can navigate from an aggregated spike to the sanitized trace and follow the audit trail to any unmasking event.

Goals: Reduce PII exposure in long-term observability stores while preserving the ability for authorized debugging and post-incident investigation. Keep query latency within SLOs (tracing lookups must not add >50ms median), and provide an immutable access ledger for compliance. Provide UX hooks for the Console dashboards to display when a trace has been redacted and whether an unmasking event exists.

Non-goals: This ticket does not change long-term metrics retention policies for metrics ingestion pipeline (metrics retention handled by existing retention jobs). It also does not implement end-user consent workflows (handled by legal/product later).

Implementation notes:
- Ingest pipeline: extend trace enrichment stage to run a rule engine for field-level classification (PII, secrets, credentials). If flagged, apply per-field masks (hash/pseudonymize) and emit a redaction delta record to the observability audit stream.
- Retention tiers: store full sanitized spans in hot index for 30 days. After 30d, move to compressed/collapsed representation (span counts, latency histograms) and remove raw span bodies. Cold bucket still stores per-tenant bloom metadata to allow targeted rehydration when policy permits.
- Conditional unmasking: implement a reveal broker service that verifies RBAC + purpose + timebox; on approval the broker requests the encrypted KV shard containing the original sensitive fields (stored encrypted with tenant CMK), performs transient unmasking in-memory and issues a short-lived reveal token tied to the access ledger entry.
- Access ledger & audit: every reveal request must emit an immutable audit record (who, why, bounds, token id, target span ids). Ledger entries are stored in hardened append-only storage with tenant-scoped retention and an index for regulatory queries.
- Console UX: dashboard panels must indicate redaction status per timeseries and add a CTA: ‘Request unmask for selected spike’. When clicked, open the authorize dialog (select purpose, justification) and submit to broker. If approved, Console fetches the sanitized trace + ephemeral fields and overlays them with a provenance ribbon containing link to audit entry.

Acceptance criteria:
1) Ingest pipeline flags and masks at least three PII classes (email, phone, API keys) and emits redaction deltas visible in the audit stream.
2) Hot index retains sanitized spans for 30 days; cold index only contains aggregated/collapsed data after migration job runs.
3) Reveal broker enforces RBAC and emits an audit entry for any unmask operation; reveal tokens expire in <= 10 minutes.
4) Latency regression tests show median trace lookup latency increase < 50ms and p95 < 200ms in 95% of test runs.
5) Console dashboard displays redaction badges and can initiate a reveal flow and display provenance link to the ledger.

Risks & trade-offs: Storing original sensitive fields (even encrypted) increases attack surface; mitigate by tenant CMKs, HSM-backed decryption control, and strict key rotation policies. Reveal broker centralizes authorization — potential availability impact; add horizontal scaling and circuit-breaker fallback to a read-only sanitized-only mode.

Metrics to monitor: reveal_request_rate, reveal_success_rate, reveal_latency_ms, audit_write_errors, ingest_redaction_rate, hot_to_cold_migration_duration.
